text:
emily: Support case — new user tried to containerize the quickstart and the Dockerfile in docs/quickstarts/container/Dockerfile fails on older Docker and CI. They copied it verbatim and hit: "failed to parse Dockerfile: unknown flag: --chown"

ravi: which line is that? link?

emily: the Dockerfile uses `COPY --chown=1000:1000 . /app` and also uses `RUN --mount=type=ssh` in a multi-stage build. The user's CI runner is on Docker 19.03 and BuildKit disabled so both flags error out.

olga: ah, yeah. We switched to BuildKit-only optimized Dockerfile a while ago for faster builds and better layer caching, but didn't add a fallback or callout. New users just copy/paste and their pipelines explode.

emily: they also copied the .env example into the image with `COPY .env /app/.env` which caused them to accidentally bake secrets into a public image pushed to Docker Hub. Support had to walk them through rotating keys.

ravi: two fixes: 1) make the Dockerfile copy/paste safe for non-BuildKit users (avoid `--chown` and `--mount`), or provide a clearly labeled BuildKit-optimized Dockerfile and a conservative, portable Dockerfile. 2) add a big warning about not copying .env into images and show a better pattern (ARG + runtime env or mount via docker run -v or use docker secrets).

olga: agreed. Proposed portable Dockerfile snippet for quickstart: 
```
# Portable (works without BuildKit)
FROM node:18-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --silent
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM node:18-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --production --silent
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]
```
No --chown, no mounts. Also update docs to show how to pass secrets at runtime: 
```
# do NOT bake secrets into the image
# recommended: set env var at runtime
docker run -e REDWOOD_API_KEY="$REDWOOD_API_KEY" myapp:latest
# or bind-mount on local dev: docker run -v $(pwd)/.env:/app/.env:ro myapp:latest
```

emily: love that. Also add a short CI note: if you want BuildKit features, enable BuildKit and document minimal versions (Docker 20.10+ and BuildKit enabled). Provide the faster Dockerfile in a file named Dockerfile.buildkit with a short explanation in the README.

ravi: docs UX note: the copy button on the site should copy the exact code block that's labeled. We should split the quickstart page into two headings: "Portable Dockerfile (recommended for beginners/CI)" and "BuildKit-optimized Dockerfile (advanced)" so users intentionally choose.

infra-bot: Suggestion: add a linter CI check that flags `COPY .env` or `ADD .env` in Dockerfiles across the repo, and fail CI for docs changes that introduce that pattern. I can open a small action.

docs-bot: Reminder: tag PR with docs/quickstart and infra/ci. Include minimal supported versions and a short security note about not baking secrets into images. Also include a follow-up issue to check other language quickstarts for BuildKit-only features.

olga: PR #5120 opened: adds portable Dockerfile, separate BuildKit Dockerfile (Dockerfile.buildkit), explicit runtime env examples, a security callout about secrets, and a docs TOC update to label the two variants. cc @ravi @emily for review.

emily: quick review left with a tiny wording nit on the security callout. :thumbsup: once changed.

ravi: LGTM after nit. Also added an infra issue: #5121 to add the Dockerfile linter.

emily: thanks all — filing a small onboarding checklist update so quickstarts that include images have both variants and a secret-handling reminder. :white_check_mark:
